metadata.title: Darren Waller finishes with only one reception Thursday night
metadata.description: Darren Waller caught 1-of-2 targets for 11 yards in Thursday's 27-19 loss to the Packers.
metadata.analysis: Waller now has just two catches on a total of six targets over the last three weeks. Unlike in Week 7, when he scored on a 50-yard gain, the veteran TE was limited to just 11 yards in Week 8. Early on this season, it looked like Waller would be a significant contributor for the Panthers. That has now faded.

metadata.title: Darren Waller a Low-Level Fantasy Option in Tough Matchup
metadata.description: Carolina tight end Darren Waller has a very tough test awaiting in Week 8 against Green Bay on Thursday night. The Packers have been one of the toughest matchups for fantasy tight ends so far, and Waller himself hasn't delivered much, so the tight end is a low-level fantasy option for the coming week. Waller was a bit involved across the team's first four games, tallying at least two catches and 28 yards in each contest, but he's managed just one catch across the past two games combined. The reception was a 50-yard touchdown in Week 7 against Tampa Bay, so he still put up a solid fantasy score, but the bigger takeaway is his lack of involvement lately. He slots in 21st among tight ends in our RotoBaller Week 8 projections, showing he is a better option in deeper fantasy setups.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Remains an Extremely Risky Streaming Option
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller turned one of two targets into a 50-yard touchdown in Sunday's Week 7 loss to Tampa Bay, but the big play masked his limited role in a crowded tight end rotation. Waller logged just 45% of Carolina's offensive snaps, nearly identical to his 46% share in Week 6, and drew only four targets across those two games. The Panthers' tight end rotation leaves little room for optimism. Tommy Tremble played 68% of the snaps and scored twice against Philadelphia in Week 6, then saw his share fall to 48% against Tampa Bay while matching Waller with only two targets. Mitchell Evans also remains involved, logging snap shares of 54% and 50% over the past two weeks. With three tight ends competing for limited opportunities, Waller is a touchdown-or-bust desperation streamer, not a dependable fantasy option.

metadata.title: Darren Waller catches long TD in loss to Tampa
metadata.description: Darren Waller caught one of two targets for a 50-yard touchdown in the Panthers' 43-13 loss to the Buccaneers on Sunday,
metadata.analysis: If you have to only catch one ball, you might as well make it count. Waller rewarded those who started him with a long 50-yard score before going silent for the rest of the way. He's a risky start in fantasy despite some initial optimism for his role,

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Back in end zone during loss
metadata.description: Waller brought in one of two targets for a 50-yard touchdown in the Panthers' 43-13 loss to the Buccaneers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Waller's one catch not only netted Bryce Young his only passing touchdown of the day, but it also generated team-high receiving yardage. The veteran tight end's splash play naturally was a boon for his fantasy managers, but Waller has seen just four targets over the last two games after opening the season with multiple catches in each of the first four contests. Waller will take a 14-198-3 line into a Week 8 road matchup against the Packers on Thursday.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Snags Long Touchdown in Loss
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller was able to somewhat bounce back after posting a dud during last week's game. Waller ripped off a big score during Sunday's loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The veteran tight end scored a 50-yard touchdown, but that was his only catch of the game. It has not been an ideal season for Waller, who has only two games with 50 receiving yards or more heading into the Week 8 matchup against the Green Bay Packers. He's looking like a low-floor TE2 for that game.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Too Risky of a Bet in Week 7
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller needs to rebound in a big way, but it might not be enough for fantasy managers in Week 7 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The veteran's fantasy value dipped after he posted goose eggs in Week 6, catching neither of his two targets against the Philadelphia Eagles. Waller was dealing with a toe injury before that game, but did not miss any time for injury-related reasons ahead of Sunday's game against Tampa Bay. The Buccaneers have struggled against the passing game, which could lead Bryce Young to vary his targets. However, Waller's diminished target share and poor Week 6 performance make him a risky bet, even as a deep-league streaming option.

metadata.title: Darren Waller blanked in Week 6
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller did not record a reception on two targets in a Week 6 win over Philadelphia.
metadata.analysis: Waller's two targets were his fewest since Week 1. He had 14 between Weeks 3 and 4 heading into a Week 5 bye, but tight end Tommy Tremble got involved with two touchdowns in Week 6. The Panthers' offense has been potent, but Tremble has been involved as well with 11 catches in the last three games.

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Quiet in Week 6 win
metadata.description: Waller failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 25-14 win over the Eagles.
metadata.analysis: Waller dealt with a toe injury during the practice week and ended up playing behind both Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans in this one, as Tremble was the big producer in the box score, catching a pair of red-zone touchdowns. Waller is one of the many touchdown-or-bust fantasy options at the tight end position.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Looking to Remain Involved in Week 6 Game Versus Eagles
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller (toe) enters Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles with 13 receptions for 148 yards (11.4 yards per reception) and two touchdowns. He will look to continue his solid production against the Eagles. Waller is dealing with a toe injury and was limited in practice on Wednesday and Thursday before being upgraded to a full participant on Friday. He will come into Sunday's game without an injury designation and is good to go. Waller faces a Philadelphia defense that allows 238.8 passing yards per game (26th in the NFL), but, according to Pro Football Reference, only gives up 4.9 fantasy points per game to tight end (eighth in the NFL). Waller has caught both of his touchdowns in the red zone this season. He is RotoBaller's No. 18 tight end for Week 6 (half-PPR).

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Good to go
metadata.description: Waller (toe) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Philadelphia.
metadata.analysis: Waller should be fine to handle his usual role after upgrading to full practice participation Friday. He was limited Wednesday and Thursday, coming out of a Week 5 bye.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Carries No Injury Designation Into Week 6
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller (toe) practiced in full Friday and carries no injury designation into Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles, according to the team's final injury report. Waller was listed as a limited participant Wednesday and Thursday, although Wednesday's participation was only an estimate because Carolina did not practice. He has caught 13 passes for 148 yards and two touchdowns through four games, with both scores coming against Atlanta in Week 2. His involvement in the passing game has increased recently, drawing eight targets against Cleveland in Week 3 and six against Detroit in Week 4 after receiving just five combined over the first two games. However, those 14 targets produced only eight catches for 87 yards without a touchdown. With Jalen Coker also cleared to play, Waller remains a touchdown-dependent TE2 option for fantasy managers in Week 6.

metadata.title: Darren Waller (toe) limited again Thursday
metadata.description: Darren Waller (toe) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran tight end was a limited participant for another practice on Thursday. His toe injury doesn't seem to be a serious issue, but there's always a chance that it will leave him out for a week. Tommy Tremble (rib) would see more work if that's the case.

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Limited again Thursday
metadata.description: Waller (toe) remained limited at Thursday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Waller has registered back-to-back limited practice sessions coming out of Carolina's Week 5 bye. The veteran TE could avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Eagles but ramping up his participation level to full Friday. Tommy Tremble (ribs) has also opened Week 6 prep with consecutive limited practices, but both Waller and Tremble seem likely to suit up Sunday, as neither has missed a game this season.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Remains Limited With Toe Injury
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller (toe) was limited in Thursday's practice, according to Joe Person, matching his estimated participation from Wednesday's walkthrough. Waller dealt with the same injury ahead of Carolina's Week 4 victory over Detroit but was able to play, catching three passes for 36 yards. The 34-year-old has recorded 13 receptions for 148 yards and two touchdowns on 19 targets through four games, with both scores coming against Atlanta in Week 2. His involvement has increased recently, drawing 14 targets over his last two appearances and turning those opportunities into eight catches for 87 yards. That usage offers some encouragement for fantasy managers, although Waller hasn't found the end zone since Week 2. Fellow tight end Tommy Tremble (ribs) has also been limited this week, leaving Carolina with some uncertainty at the position ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. Waller remains a potential streaming option in deeper leagues.

metadata.title: Darren Waller (toe) limited at practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Darren Waller (toe) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Carolina left the veteran limited at practice on Wednesday. They are likely trying to limit his workload early on in the week, so fantasy managers shouldn't be too concerned with his availability for Week 6 at this point, unless he's downgraded at some point later on in the week.

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Tending to toe injury
metadata.description: Waller was listed as a limited participant on Wednesday's practice estimate due to a toe injury.
metadata.analysis: Waller has been a regular part of the Panthers' passing game this season, sitting on a 13-148-2 line on 19 targets through four contests. Coming out of the team's Week 5 bye, though, both Waller and fellow TE Tommy Tremble (ribs, LP) are tending to injuries, leaving some question marks in the position group. Practices Thursday and Friday likely will determine if either of them enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Philadelphia.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Carries Limited Week 6 Streaming Appeal
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller returns from his Week 5 bye having drawn 14 targets over his last two games, but a difficult matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles makes him a risky fantasy option. Waller has caught 13 of 19 targets for 148 yards and two touchdowns through four games, with both scores coming against Atlanta in Week 2. His involvement increased against Cleveland and Detroit, although those 14 targets produced only eight receptions for 87 yards. Waller also played just 53% of Carolina's offensive snaps against the Lions, with Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans continuing to see substantial playing time. The Panthers could also welcome back Jalen Coker (quadriceps), who is reportedly on track to return after missing Week 4. Philadelphia has generally defended opposing tight ends well, adding another obstacle for a player whose fantasy production has been inconsistent outside his two-touchdown outing. Rostered in just 16% of leagues, Waller remains worth considering in 14-team formats, but his uncertain workload makes him a touchdown-dependent streaming option rather than a priority waiver addition.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Could Hit Waiver Wires with Panthers on Bye
metadata.description: In a Week 4 win played without one of the team's leading receivers, Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller caught only three passes for 36 yards. With Jalen Coker (quadriceps) sidelined by a quadriceps injury, the passing offense was funneled primarily through second-year receiver Tetairoa McMillan, who set or matched career highs across the board with 14 receptions on 16 targets, 192 yards, and two touchdowns. Still, despite a quiet outing, Waller remains a critical piece of one of the league's most improved offenses. Following a disappointing performance, and with the Panthers on a Week 5 bye, he is likely to hit waivers in a number of leagues, making the 34-year-old veteran an intriguing stash candidate for contending teams with adequate bench space. Unfortunately, the Panthers face an Eagles team in Week 6 that has been the most difficult tight end matchup through the first month of the season.

metadata.title: Darren Waller catches three passes Sunday night
metadata.description: Darren Waller hauled in 3-of-6 targets for 36 yards in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
metadata.analysis: In a game where Bryce Young cleared 300 yards passing and two of Carolina's top three wide receivers were out with injury, much more should have been expected from Waller. However, nearly half of Young's completions went to Tetairoa McMillan, who finished with almost 200 yards and a pair of touchdowns. That just did not leave much for Waller or any other Carolina route runner. The veteran remains a TD-dependent TE2.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Comes Up Short in Favorable Spot
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller had a favorable setup Sunday night and did very little with it. Waller caught three of six targets for 36 yards in the 32-26 win over Detroit, a disappointing result against a defense that had already allowed six touchdowns to tight ends through three games. The opportunity was there, too. Carolina played without Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette, while Bryce Young threw 41 passes for 329 yards. Waller still finished well behind Tetairoa McMillan, who dominated the passing game with 14 catches for 192 yards and two touchdowns. The veteran also played only 53% of the offensive snaps as Mitchell Evans and Tommy Tremble remained heavily involved. Waller has now gone two straight games without a touchdown after scoring twice in Week 2. With Carolina heading into its bye, his fantasy stock has cooled considerably.

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Held to three catches on SNF
metadata.description: Waller caught three of six targets for 36 yards in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
metadata.analysis: Waller finished second on the Panthers in targets and was one yard behind John Metchie for second on the team in receiving yards, but Tetairoa McMillan (14 catches for 192 yards and two TDs on 16 targets) was the clear No. 1 option in the passing game as the Panthers played without starting wide receiver Jalen Coker (quadriceps). The Lions had given up a league-high six touchdowns to tight ends entering play Sunday, but Waller was unable to add to that total. Waller and the Panthers will be on bye in Week 5 before facing the Eagles in Week 6.

metadata.title: Darren Waller a Priority Streaming Option in Week 4
metadata.description: The Carolina Panthers' receiver room is battling injuries, but tight end Darren Waller should see more targets in Week 4. Waller was dealing with a toe injury leading up to Week 4, but was off the injury list and a full practice participant on Friday. The veteran has hauled in 10 receptions on 13 targets for 112 yards this season, and his target share should spike in Week 4 since receiver Xavier Legette (knee) is out and Jalen Coker (quad) is questionable to play. Detroit has struggled to contain tight ends this season and is allowing a league-high 299.3 passing yards per game. Even if Coker plays, Waller is a priority streaming option against a struggling Detroit D.

metadata.description: Darren Waller (rest) practiced in a full capacity on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The Panthers gave the veteran Wednesday off as a rest day, but he was back at practice on Thursday and participated in a full capacity. He should be a full go for this week's matchup against the Detroit Lions on Sunday.

metadata.title: Darren Waller (rest) returns to practice Thursday
metadata.description: Darren Waller returned to practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Waller got a rest day from practice to open the week on Wednesday. He remains a TE2 for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Darren Waller (rest) absent from practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Darren Waller (rest) did not take part in Carolina's practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: As usual, Waller was given Wednesday off as a veteran rest day. He should be back at practice on Thursday and projects to be a full go for Week 4, assuming he suffers no injuries throughout the week.

metadata.title: Darren Waller a Premier Tight End Streamer Ahead of Week 4
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller was heavily involved in his team's passing game in their Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns, recording five catches for 51 yards on eight targets. The 34-year-old has gotten off to a solid start to the season, hauling in 10 receptions for 112 yards and two touchdowns on 13 targets across three games. Waller's increased usage came after Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker (quad) left the game with a quad strain. Coker reportedly avoided serious injury, but his status for Carolina's Week 4 matchup against the Detroit Lions is up in the air. Even if Coker plays, Waller could be in position for a big game in Week 4. The Lions' pass defense has really struggled to begin 2026 and has already given up six receiving touchdowns to tight ends this season. In leagues where he's available on the waiver wire, Waller profiles as a priority tight end streamer for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Darren Waller hauls in five passes Sunday
metadata.description: Darren Waller hauled in 5-of-8 targets for 51 yards in Sunday's 21-18 loss to the Cleveland Browns.
metadata.analysis: Waller was one of the few bright spots for the Panthers on Sunday. He led the team in targets and was able to finish with five catches for over 50 yards, though that wasn't enough to lead them to a win over the Browns. He can be safely started in PPR leagues moving forward.

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Continues producing in loss
metadata.description: Waller brought in five of eight targets for 51 yards in the Panthers' 21-18 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Waller continued to click frequently with Bryce Young, leading the Panthers in receptions and targets while finishing second in receiving yards with totals that all qualified as season highs. The veteran tight end has proven to be a seamless fit in head coach Dave Canales' offense, recording 10 receptions for 112 yards and two touchdowns on 13 targets over the first three games. Waller should continue to fill a prominent role in a Week 4 home matchup against the high-powered Lions next Sunday night.

metadata.title: Darren Waller a Red-Zone Threat in Week 3
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller is a touchdown threat in Week 3 against the Cleveland Browns. Waller's receiving volume figures to stay low, but if you are in dire need of a start at the position, Waller could deliver. The Panthers should find themselves in scoring position often on Sunday, and the team clearly wants to get Waller heavily involved around the goal line. He scored two touchdowns in Week 2 and had a touchdown called back due to a penalty in Week 1. Waller has yet to earn more than three targets in a game this season, so he is very touchdown-dependent. However, he is about as good a bet as anyone to score a touchdown in Week 3. Additionally, Cleveland has allowed at least 8.8 fantasy points to the opposing team's starting tight end in each game this season. If you are struggling with poor play at tight end, Waller could provide streaming value this week.

metadata.title: Darren Waller (rest) returns to practice Thursday
metadata.description: Darren Waller (rest) returned to practice and was a full participant on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: As expected, the veteran was back at practice on Thursday after getting the day off on Wednesday as a veteran rest day. He should be a full go for Week 3 and will continue to have touchdown upside on a week-to-week basis moving forward.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Showing Great Red-Zone Chemistry with his QB
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller has shown a strong connection with Bryce Young in his first two games with the Panthers, making an immediate impact after joining the team in August. He didn't play in the preseason, but when the games started to count, he became a prime option for Carolina in the red zone. Waller had a short touchdown called back due to a penalty in Week 1, but he found the end zone twice in Week 2. The 34-year-old caught all five of his targets for 61 yards in his two games and will continue to be a go-to option in the red zone due to his ability to win contested catches. He only played 35% of the team's snaps in Week 1 and 44% of the snaps in Week 2, so there is also the potential for more growth in other areas of the field as he settles into the team's offense. Waller is definitely a tight end on the rise and is a pickup to consider in all formats if you need tight end help. This week, he and the Panthers visit the Browns in Cleveland.

metadata.title: Darren Waller (rest) a non-participant Wednesday
metadata.description: Darren Waller (rest) was a non-participant at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: To no surprise, Carolina gave Waller the day off on Wednesday as a veteran rest day. He should be back at practice on Thursday and is expected to be a full go for Week 3 at this point.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Has Played His Way onto 12-Team Rosters
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller made the most of limited work Sunday, catching all three of his targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns in a 34-3 win over Atlanta. The touchdowns will get the attention, but the role still needs some context. Waller played 29 offensive snaps, or 44%, while Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans both played more. That was still a step up from Week 1, when Waller logged 24 snaps and had a touchdown wiped out by penalty. Carolina clearly has a use for him near the goal line, and this is not new territory. Waller scored six times on only 24 catches for Miami last season. The volume may stay frustrating, but tight end is thin enough that those scoring chances matter. RotoBaller's Week 3 waiver coverage has him as an add in 12-team leagues, with one column calling him a must-add at that depth. He is worth picking up now, but managers should expect some low-target weeks along the way.

metadata.title: Darren Waller snags two touchdown passes in win
metadata.description: Darren Waller caught all three of his targets for 33 yards and two scores in the Panthers' 34-3 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Waller had himself a great fantasy day, heavily boosted by the two touchdowns. He's only had five targets so far this year, but if the Panthers are willing to use him in the red zone, he's worth a look for those needing a tight end streamer.

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Two TD grabs in rout of Atlanta
metadata.description: Waller caught all three of his targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers' 34-3 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Waller had a touchdown called back in Week 1 against the Bears on an offensive pass interference, but he made a pair of red-zone catches count in this one, scoring from seven and 12 yards. It's become evident that Carolina has big plans for Waller in the scoring area this season. He's not going to go for many yards most weeks, but he's always a candidate to get into the end zone. Waller gets a plus Week 3 draw against the Browns next Sunday.

metadata.title: Darren Waller a Boom-or-Bust Tight End Option Vs. Atlanta
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller caught both of his targets for 28 receiving yards in last Sunday's 59-37 loss to the Chicago Bears. The 34-year-old did have a one-yard touchdown called back on a penalty. Waller signed a one-year, $1.3 million contract with the Panthers during training camp and did not play a preseason game. He will look to build chemistry with quarterback Bryce Young as he continues to learn Carolina's offense. The veteran TE is a boom-or-bust option in fantasy as he rotated with Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans throughout Week 1. Waller logged 24 snaps compared to Tremble's 34 and Evans' 27. Waller is touchdown-dependent and is an option in very deep leagues, and is RotoBaller's TE32 in the latest Week 2 rankings.

metadata.title: Darren Waller (rest) returns to practice Thursday
metadata.description: Darren Waller (rest) returned to practice as a full participant on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: As expected, the veteran tight end was back and practicing at full capacity for the Panthers on Thursday. He should play in Week 2 but shouldn't be considered a reliable fantasy option at this point in the season.

metadata.title: Darren Waller (rest) misses practice on Wednesday
metadata.description: Darren Waller (rest) missed Carolina's practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: To no surprise, the veteran tight end was given the day off on Wednesday as a veteran rest day. He should be back at practice on Thursday and is expected to be a full go in Week 2, although he shouldn't be started in most league formats at this point after a disappointing start to the season last week.

metadata.title: Darren Waller catches two passes in Week 1 loss
metadata.description: Darren Waller caught both of his targets for 28 yards in the Panthers' 59-37 loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 1.
metadata.analysis: Waller made the most of his minimal involvement in a Carolina passing attack that saw the ball spread to seven different receivers in the season opener, averaging 14.0 yards per reception in the loss. The tight end will look for more involvement in a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Goes for 28 yards in Week 1
metadata.description: Waller secured both of his targets for 28 yards in the Panthers' 59-37 loss to the Bears on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Waller actually had a one-yard touchdown called back on a penalty on the Panthers' opening drive. Carolina used all three of Tommy Tremble, Mitchell Evans and Waller pretty heavily against Chicago, and both Tremble and Waller each ran 18 routes. Waller isn't going to be a full-time player, but it's clear he's going to be featured in the scoring area. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet most weeks and gets a road date with the Falcons next Sunday.

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Suiting up Sunday
metadata.description: Waller is listed as active for Sunday's season opener against the Bears.
metadata.analysis: Waller had been preparing to play Week 1, and he will indeed occupy a spot on the active roster. It remains to be seen what role he will fill, though, as fellow tight ends Tommy Tremble, Mitchell Evans and Feleipe Franks will also be in uniform.
